Change c0140. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. VI; 1831 Ch. VII.

Context before (unchanged): Clerval spoke thus as we hurried through the streets; the words impressed themselves on my mind, and I remembered them afterwards in solitude.

1818 text: But now, as soon as the horses arrived, I hurried into a cabriole, and bade farewell to my friend.

1831 text: But now, as soon as the horses arrived, I hurried into a cabriolet, and bade farewell to my friend.

Diff: But now, as soon as the horses arrived, I hurried into a [-cabriole-] {+cabriolet+} , and bade farewell to my friend.

result.rationale: "cabriole" becomes "cabriolet": the same carriage, spelled in the standard form. The vehicle, action and meaning are unchanged, so this is an orthographic or lexical variant with no interpretive consequence.
